Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel, for the petitioners.
2. Ms. Sweta Badola, learned Brief Holder, for the State of Uttarakhand.

3. By means of the present writ petition, the petitioners had impugned the First Information Report No.234 of 2024, dated 17.10.2024, under Sections 232, 498A of IPC and Section  of the Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, registered with Police Station Rajpur, District Dehradun.

4. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioner nos.1 and 2, are father-in-law and mother-in-law of the respondent no.3, while petitioner nos.3 and 4 are brother-in- law (Devar) and sister-in-law (Devarani) of the respondent no.3.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the allegations in the impugned FIR are quite general in nature, and even prima facie they do not form an offence of harassment towards the demand of dowry.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners are resident of Meerut and the First Information Report is lodged in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, which would add inconvenience to the petitioners.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the tone and tenor of the FIR reflects as alleged by the complainant against the petitioners and her husband, appears to be something done with own free will of the respondent no.3, subsequently was given a colour of demand of dowry and harassment.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that since the petitioners are resident of Meerut, and especially petitioner nos.1 and 2 are aged persons, they could be extended the benefit of the proviso to Section 180 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and under which their statement may be recorded through audio visual electronic mode.
6. Per contra
learned

counsel for the State submits that the allegations in the FIR are serious in nature, and for supporting the case of the respondent no.3, and respondent no.3 is required to be issued notice by this Court.

1 7.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the FIR, this Court is of the opinion that the allegations in the FIR are quite general so far as the present petitioners are concerned, and therefore, they deserve protection by this Court.
8. Issue notice to the respondent no.3, returnable within four weeks'.
Steps to be taken within three days.
Respondents may file their counter affidavit within three weeks'.
In the meantime, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners pursuant to the FIR No.0234 of 2024, dated 17.10.2024, provided the petitioners cooperate with the investigation.
It is also provided that the Investigating Officer may record the statement of the petitioners by audio visual electronic mode.

( Pa nk a j Pur ohit , J.) 05.12.2024 NR/
